subject: Arabic
source: Drive: Curriculum/Arabic folder and Secondary Lesson Plan - Arabic - Y8 (format and approach); Madinah-style progression (haadhaa/dhaalika, adjectives, possessives); National Curriculum KS2 languages

lessons.title: This and that: haadhaa and dhaalika
objectives: Use haadhaa (this) for near things and dhaalika (that) for far things
Use haadhihi and tilka for feminine words
Read and say sentences with short vowels
starter: Say 'This is a book' and 'This is a ruler' in Arabic.
Which word means 'door': baab or bayt?

teach.heading: Bismillah and Arabic revision
teach.note: Begin with bismillah and a quick revision of haadhaa/haadhihi. Pupils say the sentence for objects held up. Establish that today they learn how to point to things that are far away.

teach.heading: Near and far
teach.note: Use a physical action: point to something close (haadhaa) then reach out and point at something far (dhaalika). Say haadhaa kitaab (close) and dhaalika bayt (far). Show a picture where the house is far away. Pupils echo.

teach.heading: Feminine near and far
teach.note: Teach tilka as the far word for girl words. Misconception: pupils say dhaalika for all far things. Use colour coding: blue for masculine, pink for feminine. Pupils practise with pairs of cards.

teach.heading: Mosque and house
bullets: Which is near? Which is far?
teach.note: Show a picture with a mosque near and a house far. Ask pupils to say the sentence. Then reverse. Use the context of the local masjid to connect to their lives. Encourage clear pronunciation of the long 'ee' in masjid and the soft 'dh' in dhaalika.

teach.heading: Sentence practice
teach.note: Have pupils read the three sentences aloud as a class, then in pairs. Ask them to translate each into English. Praise accurate vowels and ending sounds. Pupils copy one sentence in neat Arabic handwriting.

practice: Point to near and far pictures; class says haadhaa/dhaalika.
Choose haadhihi or tilka for a pencil case that is far away.
Describe pictures: near or far, masculine or feminine.
Say a sentence with the right word for each picture.
independent: Complete the sentences with هَذَا / ذَلِكَ / هَذِهِ / تِلْكَ: ___ مَسْجِدٌ (far); ___ حَقِيبَةٌ (near).
Draw a picture with one near thing and one far thing and write two sentences.
Practise reading sentences aloud with a partner.
exit: Which word means 'that' for a masculine word?
Say 'That is a house' in Arabic.
lessons.homework: Look around your home and write three sentences using haadhaa/haadhihi (near) and dhaalika/tilka (far).
lessons.send: SEND: colour-coded cards and sentence strips, pair with a buddy. EAL: provide a bilingual word bank. Stretch: add a colour word, e.g. ذَلِكَ بَيْتٌ أَبْيَضُ.

lessons.title: Describing things: big, small, new and old
objectives: Use four adjectives with masculine nouns
Put the adjective after the noun
starter: Say 'This is a mosque' in Arabic.
Say 'That is a house' in Arabic.
What is the difference between haadhaa and dhaalika?

teach.heading: Describing words
teach.note: Use hand gestures: wide arms for big, finger and thumb close for small. Pupils echo and add gestures. Ask: what is big in your house? what is small? Use objects they know.

teach.heading: New and old
teach.note: Hold up a new notebook and an old one. Use the sentence: haadhaa kitaab jadeed. Pupils say the sentence. Highlight that jadeed and qadeem end in ‘-eed’/’-eem’, a long 'ee' sound.

teach.heading: Adjective after the noun
teach.note: In English the adjective comes before the noun (big house). In Arabic it comes after (bayt kabeer). Common error: putting it first. Use two coloured cards and place them in the right order. Pupils rearrange the cards.

teach.heading: Making more sentences
teach.note: Pupils read each sentence, then translate. Pronounce carefully. Ask: how do you know these are masculine? (haadhaa/dhaalika and the nouns). Quick game: teacher says an English description, pupils find the Arabic.

teach.heading: Match and say
teach.note: Give a bank of pictures: big house, small car, new pen, old book. Pupils match and say sentences using haadhaa. Walk around breakout rooms and check word order.

practice: Show a picture of a big house; pupils say haadhaa bayt kabeer.
Match opposite words: kabeer/sagheer and jadeed/qadeem.
Describe three pictures using haadhaa + noun + adjective.
Pair task: one pupil draws, the partner says the sentence.
independent: Write four sentences about masculine things using the adjectives.
Draw a big mosque and a small house; label with Arabic sentences.
exit: Where does the adjective go: before or after the noun?
lessons.homework: Write two sentences about two objects at home: one new and one old (e.g. هَذَا كِتَابٌ قَدِيمٌ).
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards with Arabic labels and colour-coded endings. EAL: provide bilingual flashcards. Stretch: add two adjectives to one noun with wa, e.g. بَيْتٌ كَبِيرٌ وَجَدِيدٌ.

lessons.title: Describing girl words: big, small, beautiful
objectives: Make adjectives feminine by adding ة
Say sentences with feminine nouns and adjectives
starter: Say 'that is a new book' in Arabic.

teach.heading: Feminine nouns
teach.note: Show pictures. Recall that most feminine nouns end in ة. Pupils spot the round ending on the board. Ask them to find ة in each word.

teach.heading: Feminine adjectives
teach.note: Show the pattern: add ة to the adjective to describe a girl word. Use arrow animation. Misconception: pupils forget to change the adjective. Insist: girl word, girl adjective.

teach.heading: Beautiful
bullets: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty
teach.note: Teach jameel/jameela. Authentic hadith: 'Allah is beautiful and loves beauty' (Sahih Muslim). Link to noticing beauty in creation. Practise: hadeeqa jameela.

teach.heading: Making sentences
teach.note: Pupils read in chorus, then pairs. Translate the sentences. Pupils point to the ة endings on both words. Highlight the match: both words end with ة.

teach.heading: Boy or girl sentence?
teach.note: Compare boy and girl sentences side by side. Ask: what changes? (haadhihi, ة twice). Play a game: teacher says a noun, pupils say the full sentence with an adjective of their choice.

practice: Recall the six adjectives we have learned.
Say 'this is a big house' and 'that is a new pen' in Arabic.
Describe pictures with feminine nouns and adjectives.
Fix mistakes: هَذِهِ سَيَّارَةٌ كَبِيرٌ → correct it.
independent: Write three sentences with feminine nouns.
Draw a beautiful garden and write a sentence.
lessons.homework: Write four sentences describing things at home using haadhaa/haadhihi and an adjective.
lessons.send: SEND: use sentence frames with the two options highlighted. EAL: read sentences aloud in pairs with a buddy. Stretch: write a short description of your room using at least three adjectives.

lessons.title: My book, your book: possessives
objectives: Say 'my' with nouns using the ending -ee
Say 'your' for a boy and for a girl
starter: Say 'this is a small room' in Arabic.

teach.heading: My things
teach.note: Explain: adding -ee to the end of a noun makes it 'my'. Hold up your own book: kitaabee. Pupils hold up theirs. Spell out the Arabic ending ـِي.

teach.heading: Girl words and my
teach.note: Show that the round ة changes to ت before ـِي. Say haqeebatee and mistaratee. This is a common point of confusion; keep to a few examples and do repeated drills.

teach.heading: Your things
bullets: Look at who you talk to
teach.note: Use two name cards: a boy's name and a girl's name, each beside a book. Point to each book: kitaabuka / kitaabuki. Explain -ka for a boy and -ki for a girl; we met these in maa ismuka/ismuki.

teach.heading: Whose is it?
teach.note: Introduce the question 'liman haadhaa l-kitaab?' Practise a short dialogue with props. Pupils say: haadhaa kitaabee. If it is a girl word: haadhihi haqeebatee.

teach.heading: Class sentences
teach.note: Practise in a circle: pupils pass items and say the sentence. Pay attention to haadhaa/haadhihi. Praise for correct changes of ة to ت.

practice: Describe three pictures with a noun and an adjective.
Which adjective ending do we add to a girl word?
Say 'my book' and 'my bag' in Arabic with objects.
independent: Write six phrases: kitaabee, qalamee, haqeebatee, mistaratee, kitaabuka, kitaabuki (in Arabic script).
Draw your school bag and label five things 'my ...' in Arabic.
exit: How do you say 'my pen' in Arabic?
What happens to the ة in 'haqeeba' when we say 'my bag'?
lessons.homework: Make a poster of five things you own labelled in Arabic with 'my'.
lessons.send: SEND: use picture cards and fewer words, reinforce with objects. EAL: compare with home-language possessives. Stretch: write dialogues with 'your' for a boy and a girl.
